front: Give three features that favor athletic remodeling over HCM in the '13–15 mm wall thickness gray zone.'
back: Normal (or larger) LV cavity size, preserved diastolic function with normal or supernormal e′, and reversal of the hypertrophy after 3–6 months of deconditioning. Also absence of family history of SCD, normal ECG, symmetric hypertrophy, no LGE on cMRI.

front: Give three features that favor HCM over athletic remodeling.
back: Family history of HCM or SCD, asymmetric septal hypertrophy, wall thickness > 15 mm, small LV cavity, reduced e′ velocity, abnormal ECG, and LGE on cMRI.

front: Relative wall thickness cutoff most sensitive/specific for athletic heart?
back: RWT < 0.6 (eccentric remodeling — chamber grows more than wall thickens). Contrasts with concentric hypertrophy of HCM.

front: How does an endurance athlete's right ventricle appear on echo, and how do you distinguish from ARVC?
back: Chamber dilation is common with preserved global function, no regional wall-motion abnormalities, and no aneurysms. ARVC shows regional dysfunction (RV free-wall aneurysms/microaneurysms), reduced FAC (< 33%), epsilon wave, and family history.
